name: Jealousy & Envy
overview: Scripture reveals the destructive nature of jealousy and envy through the early examples of Cain and Abel, where Cain's anger and fallen countenance led him to kill his brother after God favored Abel's offering. The account of Eve desiring the forbidden fruit highlights how craving what is not permitted can lead to sin. Additionally, Lot's choice of the well-watered plain of Jordan illustrates how envy or attraction to worldly abundance can influence decisions with significant consequences. These passages demonstrate that jealousy and envy arise from misplaced desires and can provoke sinful actions, underscoring the need for Christ-centered contentment and obedience.
